name: Diabetic Foot Ulcer
definition: Full-thickness skin ulcer of the foot in a person with diabetes, commonly related to neuropathy, pressure, deformity and/or ischemia, with substantial infection and amputation risk.

redFlags.item: Spreading infection, systemic toxicity or sepsis
Deep abscess, necrosis or suspected osteomyelitis

investigations.principle: Assess infection, perfusion and depth; obtain labs/cultures/imaging according to severity.
investigations.MRI: MRI is useful for suspected osteomyelitis when diagnosis remains uncertain.
investigations.radiographs: Plain radiographs assess bone destruction, gas or foreign body but early osteomyelitis may be occult.

amber: Antibiotics are for clinically infected ulcers, not uninfected wounds; debridement/revascularization/surgery depend on severity.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vrana/Dushta-vrana principles may be considered only alongside modern infection, vascular and diabetic-foot management.

patientEducation.summary: Full-thickness skin ulcer of the foot in a person with diabetes, commonly related to neuropathy, pressure, deformity and/or ischemia, with substantial infection and amputation risk.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.

sources.title: Guidelines on prevention and management of diabetes-related foot disease
